metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Serbia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results from the PISA 2022 Database for creative thinking. The underlying PISA assessment uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design to obtain population-representative samples of 15-year-olds within participating countries/economies; analysts working with the microdata should apply the provided student/sampling weights (and, where available, replicate weights) to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals. The factsheet itself does not specify which weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight procedures were used for the displayed estimates, so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the excerpt. Plausible values are not described in this factsheet because it focuses on score summaries, proficiency levels, and relative performance; therefore, users should consult the PISA 2022 technical documentation for the official PV and variance-estimation procedures used in the database tables referenced (e.g., III.B1.2.1, III.B1.2.2, III.B1.4.3, III.B1.5.*).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a country factsheet summarising published PISA 2022 results (means, correlations, proficiency levels, and relative success) rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with an explicit PV estimation procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported in the excerpt because the factsheet does not describe any microdata preprocessing or imputation/deletion strategy; such details are typically provided in the PISA technical documentation and database methodology rather than in the factsheet narrative.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Serbia-specific results for students who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment (in the context of the PISA 2022 main assessment cycle). It states that 6,413 students in 183 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 59,300 15-year-olds; the analytic subset is therefore the Serbia sample of students who completed the relevant PISA assessment components used to produce the creative thinking results.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarises Serbia’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Serbia’s mean creative thinking score is 29 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution (65% at Level 3 or above; 17% at Level 5 or 6) and relative strengths/weaknesses across ideation processes and domain contexts, including higher relative performance in generating creative ideas and in written/visual expression. It further documents within-Serbia gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance, but it does not present an original ML modelling pipeline or predictive metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is treated as an OECD PISA results factsheet rather than an empirical ML paper: it reports descriptive and comparative statistics from the PISA 2022 Database (with table references) and does not specify any student-level modelling, algorithmic training, or evaluation procedure. Consequently, fields required for predictive ML studies (e.g., main_findings with target-variable prediction, ML techniques, and conceptual predictor lists) are intentionally left empty. The document also does not provide microdata preprocessing details (e.g., PV combination rules or missing-data handling), which are expected to be documented in the PISA 2022 technical documentation and database methodology.
